rows.description: State Farm Arena construction
rows.note: 3% car-rental tax paid for $62.5M of public infrastructure (Bond Buyer: $70.7M car-rental-tax bonds sold 1996, refunded 2005). Arena itself financed by $130.75M Recreation Authority bonds repaid by Turner ($12.5M/yr) -> treated as private (conduit). Time Warner $20M toward infrastructure.

rows.description: 2017-18 renovation
rows.note: City $142.5M = $110M rental-car-tax bonds (tax extended to 2047) + $12.5M Turner Field sale + $20M property sales (public asset sales counted as general); Hawks $50M + overruns

rows.description: Barclays Center construction
rows.note: City capital contribution "has grown from $100 million to $205 million" (b, IBO testimony May 2009) + State $100M (c, Doctoroff via Gotham Gazette), for land acquisition and infrastructure for the arena block, outside the arena cost. MTA Vanderbilt Yard: IBO (Sept 2009) puts the subsidy at the $50M gap between Extell's $150M cash bid and Forest City's $100M and attributes $10M (present value) of it to the arena, using the 2009 terms' $20M of $100M for the arena block (b) -> land bucket (a public asset sold below the competing bid). Extell's $150M is computed from IBO's $50M gap (a). Whole-project alternatives, not counted: $50M bid gap (b); IBO's $214M appraisal ($214.5M per Atlantic Yards Report, c) minus the $100M present value of the 2009 payment stream at the MTA's 6.5% = $114.0M (a); replacement yard cut from $240-250M (MTA CFO via Atlantic Yards Report, c) or $182M (developer's figure via Atlantic Yards Report, c) to $147M (b, MTA staff summary) = $35M-$103M (a). The $10M is a present value as of FY2010 but is deflated with the construction money at the 2012 opening year (at 2010 it would be about $0.7M higher in 2026 dollars).

rows.description: 2025-26 renovation
rows.note: Estimated $150M by 2026 (private)

rows.description: TD Garden construction
rows.note: No public construction money found. Financed by a $120M bank loan and $40M developer equity (BRA 1992); the Commonwealth paid compensation for taking the developer's 150 Causeway St leasehold (not a subsidy). Approved as a Chapter 121A project with negotiated tax payments of $1.0M a year rising $0.1M a year to $1.5M, which the BRA called necessary for the financing (not quantified as a break). The 1993 House bill had the developer repay $5.126M of MBTA work by a note starting in year 11 (deferred, not a grant; enacted text not checked).

rows.description: 2019 "Legendary Transformation" expansion
rows.note: $100M Jacobs family investment (private)

rows.description: Spectrum Center construction
rows.note: City ACFR FY2020: the project "was funded primarily through a combination of installment financing obligations supported by a portion of an occupancy tax and a dedicated rental car tax, private contributions and the sale of City assets" (b, no amounts). Carolina Journal: taxpayers ~$170M, owner Johnson ~$23M (c). 2002 plan also had banks/utility underwrite $100M recovered ~$50M via sale of city land, a 3% seat tax (~$15M) and $16.8M F&B rights. $170M used as the explicitly attributed figure.

rows.description: United Center construction
rows.note: Privately financed. The 1989 state law (P.A. 86-110) valued the arena by a formula (20% of 4 x owners' net income after interest, income taxes and capital repairs) with a $1M minimum tax, for 22 years after the base year; taxes forgone 2002-2016 estimated at $46.6M nominal (expanded total only; 1994-2001 not computed). 2024 Board of Review cut AV from $92.1M to $50.3M on owner appeal.

rows.description: Rocket Arena construction
rows.note: Gateway FY1999 audit Note 7D: Cuyahoga County issued $75M (1992) and $45M (1994) of taxable economic development revenue bonds and lent the proceeds to Gateway "to pay Arena construction costs" ($120M is the par of the two issues; the $161.5M owed at Dec 31 1999 included about $45.1M of interest and $3.6M of financing costs, leaving about $112.8M of principal, a); Gateway "does not expect to be able to pay back" the county notes (FY2024 audit) -> public; repayment source not documented -> mixed. The 1990 bonds (~$148M, sin-tax backed per press) paid "primarily" for the stadium, so the earlier attribution of $100M of sin-tax bonds to the arena (PFM) is not used. Cavaliers advanced $7.8M for arena overruns, $7M later forgiven (private).

rows.description: 2017-19 "Transformation"
rows.note: County $70M principal (>= $160M with interest per Axios); Cavs $115M

rows.description: 2019 capital repairs (lease obligation)
rows.note: County sin-tax-backed bonds for Gateway capital repairs; lease makes public pay repairs > $500K

rows.description: 2024-25 major capital repairs (arena half)
rows.note: City paid Gateway $20M (Dec 2024; source fund not stated) and the County $20.0M (Jan 16 2025: Sports Facilities Improvement notes $14.2M, General Fund $2.85M, 2017B indenture fund $2.95M) for Major Capital Repairs, divided equally between the ballpark and the arena (b). Arena half counted without the County's $2.95M from the 2017B indenture fund, which may be money already counted: 10.0 + (14.2025 + 2.85)/2 = 18.53 (a). Gateway owed the Cavaliers $15.17M for repairs they advanced, probably repaid from this money (not added)

rows.description: American Airlines Center construction
rows.note: City share capped at $125M, repaid by 2% hotel-occupancy + 5% car-rental taxes approved by voters (1998, 62,861-61,237); teams (Hicks/Cuban) paid the rest.

rows.description: Ball Arena construction
rows.note: Denver Urban Renewal Authority: $36.5M developer reimbursement through TIF (demolition, remediation, site work; repaid 2016) + $4.5M City funds for public infrastructure. The 1997 Arena Agreement also gave: city title to the land with a 23-year ground lease back at $10 a year; payments based on the arena's property tax increment (the "rebates on property taxes for a 23-year term" in Ascent's FY1998 10-K, which appear to be the DURA reimbursement above, repaid in 2016, not a separate break); sales and use tax rebates during construction (amount not found); $2.25M of city business incentive payments during construction (s.5.9; relation to the $4.5M not established, not added); and exemption from the city's admissions (seat) tax (s.5.7; memo estimate only, not counted).

rows.description: $135M renovation announced Sept 2026 (to 2028-29)
rows.note: Private (KSE); planned, not counted

rows.description: Little Caesars Arena construction
rows.note: MSF Series 2014A $250M (repaid from DDA catalyst tax increment, incl. captured school taxes) + DDA Series 2017 $36M "to incentivize the Detroit Pistons to relocate" (NBA compliance). 2014B ($200M authorized, $188.5M drawn) was serviced by Olympia concession payments and retired by Olympia in 2017 -> private. Olympia donated land + construction valued at $47.8M.

rows.description: Chase Center construction
rows.note: Privately financed; team bought the land. City event-day costs (e.g., ~$2.5M/yr for parking control officers, SF Chronicle 2019) not counted.

rows.description: Toyota Center construction
rows.note: 2000 Letter Agreement: Sports Authority funds the $175M Arena Budget (+ garage + financing costs) from hotel-occupancy/car-rental-tax bonds; City acquires site (Marquette 2005: ~$20M land). Rockets pay overruns + up to $8M concessions, and their $8.5M/yr rent is pledged to a separate "Rent Supported Debt" issue that also financed construction, principal capped at $30.4M without the tenant's approval (b, lease App. A p.A-4) -> public figure overstates net public cost. City site and infrastructure money is a not-to-exceed $20M cash appropriation for "Site Acquisition and the Infrastructure Work" (b, 2000 Interlocal Arena Development Agreement s.2); no land/infrastructure split or funding stream stated -> infrastructure bucket. Public range in press: $125M-$175M.

rows.description: 2026 renovation
rows.note: Approved Apr 2026; ~$95M State of Texas per Mayor Whitmire (Houston Chronicle); Rockets/Fertitta rest

rows.description: Gainbridge Fieldhouse construction
rows.note: $79M "from taxes" (Indiana Encyclopedia); PFM: local 43%, excise-tax lease-rental revenue (CIB hotel/F&B/admissions taxes). Conflict not resolved: the 1997A/B bond par ($230.7M, b) exceeds the reported cost, and the CIB says the bonds are secured by lease rentals paid from pledged state and local taxes; no primary split of public and private money was found.

rows.description: 2019-22 renovation (25-yr deal)
rows.note: Public $295M (state+CIB $270M, city $25M); split by PFM shares: state ~34% via PSDA tax capture (incl. athletes income tax) -> tif; CIB excise taxes -> tourist; Pacers $65M

rows.description: Intuit Dome construction
rows.note: Privately financed. Team bought publicly owned site parcels (city, FAA/LAWA, school district) for $66.25M; no appraisal found showing a below-market price.

rows.description: Crypto.com Arena construction
rows.note: Privately financed building on city-owned land. City advanced about $70M (b, CAO) or ~$58M (c, Seattle 2017) of bonds and cash, which the developer must offset under the Gap Funding Agreement (in 2003 the developer paid the City $16.5M for shortfalls and inducement) -> treated as conduit financing, not public money.

rows.description: FedExForum construction
rows.note: City CAFR FY2005: "The total construction cost of $250,000 [thousand] is to be funded from $186,000 from Senior Lien Revenue Bonds, $20,000 from Subordinate Lien Revenue Bonds, $12,000 each by the City and the County from non-ad valorem revenues, and $20,000 from the State of Tennessee for a parking structure and intermodal transfer station." Sports Authority bonds ($206M) are repaid from seat fees, state sales-tax rebates on Grizzlies-generated taxes (2001-2031), county car-rental fees, city and county hotel-motel taxes and MLGW in-lieu-of-tax payments (FY2015 CAFR; split not documented -> mixed). City $12M for site and infrastructure, to be repaid from hotel-motel taxes (-> tourist); County $12M (general); State $20M parking structure (general). Total includes site, infrastructure and the parking structure; no team contribution in the funding table.

rows.description: $550M renovation: state funds allocated by council
rows.note: Council allocated $80M of the $230M state appropriation (repairs/reimbursement)

rows.description: $550M renovation: remainder pending new lease
rows.note: Remaining $150M state + $320M hotel-motel tax held until a long-term lease is signed. The Oct 8 2026 MSCSA agenda lists Amendment 1 to the Design, Construction & Funding Agreement and a CMAR prime agreement; press reports they were approved and names Flintco as contractor (Audacy, Yahoo); lease unsigned as of Oct 16 2026 (Daily Memphian: "very close"). Private Chapter 70 (2026) extends the Shelby County hotel-motel tax to the later of the NBA tenant leaving and June 30 2050, subject to local approval (not found). Alternative: "nearly $500 million in public tax dollars" of the $550M (Yahoo/Roundtable 2026-10-13)

method: select i.team, i.item_id, i.kind, i.description, i.year, i.status, i.core, i.spending_nominal_m, i.public_nominal_m, i.cpi_factor, i.spending_2026_m, i.public_2026_m, i.cost_label, i.public_label, i.note, coalesce((select list(s.source_id order by s.role desc, s.ord) from item_sources s where s.item_id = i.item_id and (s.role = 'public' or i.spending_nominal_m > 0)), []) as sources from items i order by i.team, case i.kind when 'construction' then 1 when 'purchase' then 2 when 'renovation' then 3 when 'ongoing' then 4 else 5 end, i.year, i.item_id
